our_title: Fortran order-strategy builder passed level count and flags swapped
ran: gcc -fsanitize=address,undefined repro/API-01/fort.c -lscotch -lscotcherr (against $W/build and $W/build64, pristine 7.0.17 ASan trees); ./fort 0 -> 'C      : c{rat=0.7,cpr=n{sep=(/(((levl)<(7))&((vert)>(240)))?...' and 'Fortran: ierr=0 c{rat=0.7,cpr=n{sep=(/(((levl)<(7))&((vert)>(240)))?...' byte-identical on both trees. Audit script (repro/fortran_audit.py, class ORDER): 95 wrappers checked against the C definition's parameter names, 104 against their own declaration order, 0 findings on 7.0.17.
severity_note: Silent loss of the level limit in every Fortran-built ordering strategy; same as the review.
upstream_change: 259f38a Bugfix: restore parameter order when calling from Fortran [report R. Perry]
first_pass_critique: Right on status and evidence, but it verified only the named wrapper; completeness of the class (any other wrapper forwarding its arguments out of order) was not checked. The audit script now covers all 244 wrappers: no other instance.
notes: Verified complete: no other wrapper of libscotch or libscotchmetis forwards its parameters in a different order than the C definition (strong check where names match, declaration-order check otherwise; the 45 wrappers without a parsed C definition are the METIS entry points and the no-argument Sizeof/mem/random routines).

our_title: Three Fortran wrappers took scalar arguments by value instead of by address
ran: gcc -fsanitize=address,undefined repro/API-05/ind.c (calls scotchfgraphinducelist_ and scotchfgraphinducepart_ with pointers) on $W/build and $W/build64: 'induceList ierr=0 vertnbr=2 edgenbr=2 (expect 2,2)' / 'inducePart ierr=0 vertnbr=2 edgenbr=2', no sanitizer report. scotchfdgraphband: source-read (b189b87 diff) plus the audit script's BYVALUE class, which flags every non-pointer wrapper parameter except the hidden Fortran string length that follows a 'char *': 0 findings on 7.0.17.
read_only: scotchfdgraphband was not executed (would need a distributed band test from Fortran); the fix is the same mechanical change as the two sequential ones and the audit script confirms no by-value parameter remains anywhere.
severity_note: Address used as a vertex count: out-of-bounds reads or crash from any Fortran caller; same as the review.
evidence: const SCOTCH_Num *                vnumnbr,    \ ... *revaptr = SCOTCH_graphInduceList (orggrafptr, *vnumnbr, vnumtab, indgrafptr); / const SCOTCH_Num *          fronlocnbr, \ ... *revaptr = SCOTCH_dgraphBand (srcgrafptr, *fronlocnbr, fronloctab, *distval, bndgrafptr);
upstream_change: b189b87 Bugfix: dereference integer values passed from the Fortran API [report R. Perry]
first_pass_critique: Correct. It did not check the rest of the tree for the same pattern; done now (BYVALUE class): none left. Note the upstream fix declares the new pointers as 'const SCOTCH_Num *' without the usual 'const' on the pointer itself (every neighbour uses 'const SCOTCH_Num * const'); cosmetic, not changed here.

our_title: DGRAPHSTAT wrapper exported scotchfDgraphstat instead of scotchfdgraphstat
ran: nm -D $W/build/lib/libptscotch.so | grep -i fdgraphstat -> 'SCOTCHFDGRAPHSTAT scotchfDgraphstat scotchfDgraphstat_ scotchfDgraphstat__' (same on build64). mpifort repro/API-09/stat_f.f90 against pristine: 'undefined reference to `scotchfdgraphstat_''. After patch 0001: links; mpirun -np 2 ./stat_f_build -> 'dgraphstat: velosum= 16 degrmax= 4' on both ranks, 32- and 64-bit; repro/API-24/par_f.f90 also calls it (ierr=0).
severity_note: Documented routine cannot be linked from Fortran; no silent misbehaviour.
first_pass_critique: Correct status, evidence and preferred option. Its patch sketch is the same one-token change. The audit script (CASE class) confirms this is the only wrapper whose two macro names disagree.

fix_options.label: A: lower-case the macro argument
fix_options.summary: SCOTCH_FORTRAN (DGRAPHSTAT, dgraphstat, ...): exports scotchfdgraphstat, _ and __ as every other wrapper.
fix_options.tested: stat_f.f90 links and runs (np 2) on 32- and 64-bit; full check + ptcheck pass on 32-bit.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Drops the never-documented mixed-case symbols; a caller that had hard-coded scotchfDgraphstat_ in an explicit interface would have to be fixed (none known).
fix_options.maintainer_fit: His own API-01/API-05 fixes are minimal one-line corrections of the wrapper with no compatibility shim (259f38a, b189b87).

fix_options.label: B: fix the name and keep a mixed-case alias
fix_options.summary: Add a second SCOTCH_FORTRAN stanza with the old lower-case argument 'Dgraphstat' forwarding to the corrected entry point.
fix_options.tested: untested: compatibility symbol not wanted; diff applies (git apply --check).
fix_options.tradeoffs: No link break for anyone who used the typo, but carries a misspelled symbol in the ABI forever.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: No precedent in the tree for alias symbols of a typo.

test_added: ; no Fortran PT-Scotch test program exists in src/check (only sequential test_scotch_mesh_build_f); adding an MPI Fortran test harness is beyond a bugfix commit. repro/API-09/stat_f.f90 and repro/API-24/par_f.f90 exercise it.

our_title: DGRAPHMAPSTAT wrapper has no ierr parameter and drops the return value
ran: mpicc -fsanitize=address,undefined repro/API-11/dmv2.c; mpirun -np 2 ./dmv2_build -> 'Fortran DGRAPHMAPSTAT ierr=-77 (sentinel -77 = never written)' on pristine 32- and 64-bit. With patch 0002, repro/API-24/par_f.f90 (Fortran, ierr preset to -77) prints 'par_f: OK' (ierr == 0, tgtnbr == 2) on both trees.
severity_note: Errors of a documented routine are silently lost by Fortran callers; also the only int-returning wrapper without ierr (audit IERR class).
evidence: SCOTCH_Num * const            cmexsumptr),  \ ... {  SCOTCH_dgraphMapStat (grafptr, mapptr, tgtnbrptr, ...
first_pass_critique: Correct, and it spotted the mapmin/mapmax doc swap (PS-API-6). Its sketch keeps the tab character that the pristine file contains in the argument list (' mapavgptr, mapdltptr,\t\t'); the maintainer's git diff shows tabs in red, so the patch replaces it with spaces.

fix_options.label: A: add the documented trailing int * revaptr
fix_options.summary: Wrapper takes 'int * const revaptr' after cmexsumptr and stores SCOTCH_dgraphMapStat()'s result, like every other int-returning wrapper.
fix_options.tested: par_f.f90 np 2 on 32/64-bit (ierr 0); ptcheck on 32-bit passes.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Callers compiled against the undocumented 16-argument form must add the argument (callers written from the manual already pass it).
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Manual is the contract; the wrapper is the one that deviates from all its neighbours (e.g. library_dgraph_stat_f.c:90 '*revaptr = SCOTCH_dgraphStat (...)').

fix_options.label: B: remove ierr from the manual
fix_options.summary: Keep the void wrapper, delete the 'integer ierr' row of p_l.tex.
fix_options.tradeoffs: No ABI change but leaves Fortran users without error reporting, unlike every other routine.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Against the uniform convention of the Fortran API (int result -> trailing ierr).

cleanup_done: tab character in the argument list replaced by spaces (same line rewritten anyway)
test_added: ; no Fortran MPI test harness in src/check. Exercised by repro/API-24/par_f.f90.

our_title: Manual lists mapmax before mapmin for scotchfdgraphmapstat; C and wrapper use mapmin first
ran: repro/fortran_audit.py DOCORDER class on 7.0.17: the only Fortran synopsis whose argument stems are a permutation of the C synopsis's (doc/src/ptscotch/p_l.tex:3123). After patch 0006: 0 DOCORDER findings.
severity_note: A Fortran caller following the manual gets the minimum and maximum swapped silently; raised from 'info' because the two values are the same type so nothing warns.
evidence:
& integer*{\it num}     & mapmax,  \\
                       & integer*{\it num}     & mapmin,  \\
first_pass_critique: Correct; the preferred option (fix the manual) is right.

fix_options.label: A: swap the two rows in the manual
fix_options.summary: mapmin then mapmax, as in library_pt.h and the wrapper.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He fixes synopses in 'Documentation fix' commits (f349192, a13ced9, 3e6d208); folded with the other synopsis fixes into one doc commit.

fix_options.label: B: swap the wrapper's arguments to match the manual
fix_options.summary: Change the wrapper so that mapmax precedes mapmin.
fix_options.tested: untested: ABI change not wanted; applies.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Breaks existing Fortran callers that followed the C order.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Would make the Fortran order differ from the C one, which the whole API avoids.

our_title: ARCHSIZE wrapper stores a SCOTCH_Num result through an int pointer
ran: repro/API-01/fort.c mode 2 on $W/build64 (pristine, -DINTSIZE64): 'sizeof(SCOTCH_Num)=8, after ARCHSIZE buf=0x5a5a5a5a00011170' (upper half of the Fortran integer*8 untouched). On 32-bit: int == SCOTCH_Num, nothing observable. With patch 0003, repro/API-24/seq_f.f90 presets archnbr = -1 (all bits set) and gets 8 / 8 / 6 after archbuild2 / archbuild0 / archltleaf on build64.
severity_note: Wrong value for every 64-bit Fortran caller of a documented routine (upper half is garbage); 32-bit builds unaffected.
first_pass_critique: Correct, and its suggestion to grep for other int*-vs-Num outputs is implemented by the audit script's RETTYPE/CTYPE/TYPE classes: ARCHSIZE is the only instance (archvar's int * flag, the *sizeof int * and the MPI_Fint communicators are correct).

fix_options.label: A: declare sizeptr as SCOTCH_Num *
fix_options.summary: One-token type change; matches the manual's 'integer*num archnbr' and the neighbouring archdomsize/archdomwght wrappers (SCOTCH_Num * const).
fix_options.tradeoffs: A 64-bit caller that had declared a plain 'integer' (against the manual) now gets 8 bytes written; that caller was already reading garbage.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Same shape as b189b87 (type of one wrapper parameter corrected to what the manual says).

fix_options.label: B: keep int *, truncate through a SCOTCH_Num temporary
fix_options.summary: Store (int) SCOTCH_archSize () so the full int is written; keeps the undocumented 'integer' ABI, loses large sizes.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Fixes the garbage upper half only for callers that (wrongly) use a 4-byte integer; still disagrees with the manual.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: The manual documents integer*num; he would not change the manual to int for a size that can exceed 2^31 with 64-bit Num.

test_added: ; no Fortran arch test in src/check; covered by repro/API-24/seq_f.f90.

our_title: Thirteen Fortran routines documented in the manuals are defined nowhere
ran: mpifort repro/API-24/missing_f.f90 against pristine $W/build: 13 'undefined reference to' (scotchfarchbuild0_, scotchfarchbuild2_, scotchfarchltleaf_, scotchfdgraphfree_, scotchfdgraphgrow_, scotchfdmapsizeof_, scotchfdmeshfree_, scotchfdordersizeof_, scotchfgraphorderload_, scotchfmapsizeof_, scotchfmeshstat_, scotchfordersizeof_, scotchfstratsizeof_). git log -S over the clone: none of the 13 ever existed in a *_f.c; the synopses were added by the doc commits 35b98f9 (6.0.5), 679109a/14bdd08 (Sizeof), 80b7f5c, 086b78a. After patches 0004 and 0007 (+ G02 0001 for the C declaration): missing_f links on 32/64-bit; seq_f.f90 ('seq_f: OK', MESHSTAT/SIZEOF lines identical to the C twin seq_c on both trees) and par_f.f90 ('par_f: OK', np 2, both trees) exercise every wrapper functionally; audit NOWRAP: 17 -> 0.
severity_note: Link-time failure of documented routines (no silent misbehaviour), but 13 of them and for 5+ years; 'low' rather than the review's 'info'.
evidence: scotchfarchbuild0 ( & doubleprecision (*)   & archdat, \\ ... (no 'ARCHBUILD0, archbuild0' in any src/libscotch/*_f.c); same for the other twelve
review_accuracy: accurate (13/13 confirmed); its two fix options are the right pair.
first_pass_critique: Status/evidence right. Its sketch 'void routine(args, int * revaptr)' for free/grow/stat is wrong for dgraphfree, dmeshfree and meshstat, whose C routines return void and therefore get no ierr (mirroring graphfree/graphstat); it also did not notice that dgraphgrow needs a new file (no library_dgraph_grow_f.c exists) and thus Makefile/CMakeLists entries, that archltleaf cannot compile without the missing library.h declaration (PS-API-2 / G02), and it found only 13 of the 17 NOWRAP entries (the other 4 are misspelled names in the manuals, see docs commit).

extra_instances.location: doc/src/scotch/s_l.tex:2113 ('scotchfarchcmplt' in section SCOTCH_archCmpltw), :2782 ('scotchfarchdomwght' in SCOTCH_archDomDist), :8660 ('metis_nodwend'), :8890 ('metis_metistodual'); doc/src/ptscotch/p_l.tex:3423 ('scotchfgraphdorderexit'), :3528 ('scotchfgraphdordersavemap')

fix_options.label: A: add the thirteen wrappers
fix_options.summary: One SCOTCH_FORTRAN stanza per routine beside its neighbours (Sizeof ones after the matching Exit wrapper, as d800b09 did; GRAPHORDERLOAD modelled on GRAPHMAPLOAD; MESHSTAT on GRAPHSTAT; DGRAPHFREE/DMESHFREE on GRAPHFREE); new library_dgraph_grow_f.c registered in Makefile and CMakeLists.txt; ARCHLTLEAF in a separate last commit because it needs library.h's declaration from G02 patch 0001.
fix_options.tested: Builds with 0 warnings on 32- and 64-bit; nm shows all symbols; missing_f links; seq_f/seq_c and par_f pass on both trees; full check + ptcheck pass on 32-bit; 64-bit Fortran check targets pass.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Purely additive ABI; 12 small functions plus one new source file.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He adds wrappers, not removes documentation: d800b09 'Added Fortran interfaces for most of the SCOTCH_*Sizeof() routines' is exactly this commit for the first batch; STYLE.md: every exported routine has a Fortran twin.

fix_options.label: B: remove the thirteen synopses from the manuals
fix_options.tradeoffs: No code, but removes functionality users were told exists and leaves the Fortran API incomplete.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Contradicts 80b7f5c/086b78a, where he documented routines because they were missing from the manual.

fix_options.label: C: archltleaf wrapper carrying its own library.h declaration
fix_options.summary: Standalone variant of patch 0007 for a series applied without G02's 0001.
fix_options.tested: untested as a diff; its content is patch 0007 + G02 0001, which were built together (g17-tmp branch).
fix_options.tradeoffs: Duplicates G02's header change; use one or the other.

our_title: Fortran METIS_PartMeshDual test never inspects objval, epart or npart

Negative: repro/BLD-20/corrupted.f90 (generated test + 'epart(1) = baseval + nparts') -> 'ERROR: main: invalid partition (1)', exit 1 with both v3 and v5 libraries; pristine ends successfully on the same corruption.
evidence:
call SCOTCHMETISNAMEFU (METIS_PartMeshDual) (ne, nn, eptr, eind, vgwt, vsize, ncommon, nparts, tpwgt, options, objval, epart, npart)
  end block

  deallocate (npart)
